title: When it is said: 'One should not speak a secret word. One should not speak a hurtful word face to face' — for what reason…
content: When it is said: 'One should not speak a secret word. One should not speak a hurtful word face to face' — for what reason was this said? Here, bhikkhus, if one knows a secret word to be untrue, false, and unbeneficial, one should, if possible, not speak that secret word. And if one knows a secret word to be true, not false, but unbeneficial, one should train oneself not to speak it. And if one knows a secret word to be true, not false, and beneficial, then one should know the time and speak that secret word. If one knows a hurtful word face to face to be untrue, false, and unbeneficial, one should, if possible, not speak that hurtful word face to face. If one knows a hurtful word face to face to be true, not false, but unbeneficial, one should train oneself not to speak it. And if one knows a hurtful word face to face to be true, not false, and beneficial, then one should know the time and speak that hurtful word face to face.

title: It leads to his own harm, bhikkhus, when gain, honor, and renown arise for Devadatta; it leads to the unhappiness of others, bhikkhus, when gain,…
content: It leads to his own harm, bhikkhus, when gain, honor, and renown arise for Devadatta; it leads to the unhappiness of others, bhikkhus, when gain, honor, and renown arise for Devadatta! Just as, bhikkhus, a banana tree, when it produces fruit, leads to its own harm; when it produces fruit, leads to the unhappiness of others. So too, bhikkhus, it leads to his own harm when gain, honor, and renown arise for Devadatta; it leads to the unhappiness of others when gain, honor, and renown arise for Devadatta. Just as, bhikkhus, a bamboo tree, when it produces fruit, leads to its own harm; when it produces fruit, leads to the unhappiness of others. So too, bhikkhus, it leads to his own harm when gain, honor, and renown arise for Devadatta.

title: The taker friend, The talker friend, The flatterer, The spendthrift. These four are not friends, Knowing this, the wise avoid them, Like a dangerous path.
content:
The taker friend,
The talker friend,
The flatterer,
The spendthrift.
These four are not friends,
Knowing this, the wise avoid them,
Like a dangerous path.

title: Bhikkhus, just as a dirty, stained cloth, if a dyer dips it in this or that dye — blue, yellow, red, or magenta — it…
content: Bhikkhus, just as a dirty, stained cloth, if a dyer dips it in this or that dye — blue, yellow, red, or magenta — it will take the dye poorly, it will be impure in color. Why is that? Because the cloth was not clean. So too, bhikkhus, a bad destination awaits a defiled mind. Bhikkhus, just as a clean, pure cloth, if a dyer dips it in this or that dye — blue, yellow, red, or magenta — it will take the dye well, it will be pure in color. Why is that? Because the cloth is clean. So too, bhikkhus, a good destination awaits an undefiled mind.

title: How, householder, is there vain hope? Here, householder, a person thinks: 'May I have such form in the future! May I have such feeling in…
content: How, householder, is there vain hope? Here, householder, a person thinks: 'May I have such form in the future! May I have such feeling in the future! May I have such perception in the future! May I have such formations in the future! May I have such consciousness in the future!' Thus, householder, is vain hope.

title: One restrained by conscience, Who can be found in the world? Who knows how to check criticism, Like a fine horse the whip? One restrained…
content:
One restrained by conscience,
Who can be found in the world?
Who knows how to check criticism,
Like a fine horse the whip?
One restrained by conscience,
Always mindful,
That one attains the result,
Suffering is destroyed,
Walking with even steps
On the uneven path.

title: Bhikkhus, when a child grows up and his faculties mature, he enjoys the full range of the five strands of sensual pleasure — forms cognizable…
content: Bhikkhus, when a child grows up and his faculties mature, he enjoys the full range of the five strands of sensual pleasure — forms cognizable by the eye that are desirable, lovely, agreeable, pleasing, stimulating sensual desire, enticing; sounds... odors... flavors... tangibles... When he sees a form with the eye, he lusts after a pleasant form and dislikes a disagreeable form; he dwells without mindfulness of the body, with a limited mind. He does not truly understand the liberation of mind and liberation by wisdom, where those evil, unwholesome states cease without remainder. Thus, for him, with regard to bodily contact, whatever feeling arises — pleasant, painful, or neither-painful-nor-pleasant — he rejoices in that feeling, welcomes it, and remains attached to it. Because he rejoices, welcomes, and is attached to that feeling, delight arises. Having delight in those feelings, he is attached. With attachment as condition, existence arises; with existence as condition, birth arises; with birth as condition, aging, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair arise. Thus is the origination of this whole mass of suffering.

title: Elder Nisabha: Having abandoned the five strands of sensual pleasure, Those truly delightful things that please the mind, With faith, I went forth to make…
content:
Elder Nisabha:

Having abandoned the five strands of sensual pleasure,
Those truly delightful things that please the mind,
With faith, I went forth to make an end of suffering.

I do not delight in death, I do not delight in life.
I await the time, mindful and clearly comprehending.

title: Elder Sunāga: Skilled in the mind's sign, knowing the taste of seclusion, Meditating, mindful, careful, he attains non-worldly happiness.
content:
Elder Sunāga:

Skilled in the mind's sign, knowing the taste of seclusion,
Meditating, mindful, careful, he attains non-worldly happiness.

title: What do you think, Ambattha? Have you heard the brahmins who are elders, senior, teachers, and ancestors say? In the past, those ascetics among the…
content: What do you think, Ambattha? Have you heard the brahmins who are elders, senior, teachers, and ancestors say? In the past, those ascetics among the brahmins, the authors of the mantras, the reciters of the mantras who sang, spoke, and compiled the sacred verses that today's brahmins sing, speak, and recite just as the former ones did. Those ascetics named Atthaka, Vāmaka, ..., Kassapa, Bhagu. Did they bathe well, groom well, keep their hair and beard well-trimmed, adorn themselves with garlands and jewels, wear white clothes, enjoy and indulge in the five strands of sensual pleasure, as you and your teacher do now?
